value.name: attorney identifies sentimental property
value.description: The attorney tells the siblings that objects of sentimental value, including a watch, should remain in place during the inventory rather than be removed.
evidence: Including objects of sentimental rather than financial value.
Including, Mr. Serrano, the watch in the upstairs study that I noticed yesterday you were looking at while we spoke about the dining room.

value.name: Daniel claims grandfather's watch
value.description: Daniel reacts to the mention of the watch by saying it belonged to his grandfather.

value.name: attorney instructs watch remain in inventory
value.description: The attorney explains that the watch will likely belong to Daniel, but only by agreement and not by being removed before the inventory is complete.
evidence: "Then it will, in all likelihood, be yours. But it will be yours by agreement among the three of you, recorded in the inventory, and not by removal in the meantime."

value.name: attorney asks all siblings to comply
value.description: The attorney says he is making the same request of all three siblings and not singling Daniel out.
evidence: "I am asking this of all of you. I am not singling you out."

value.name: attorney directs Lucia to leave letter
value.description: The attorney tells Lucia to leave the letter where she found it in the sewing room until the inventory period ends.
evidence: "Ms. Serrano, the same applies to the letter, which I would like you to leave in the sewing room where you found it for the remainder of the inventory period, after which it is, in my view as your attorney, indisputably yours."

value.name: attorney directs Rosa to leave books
value.description: The attorney tells Rosa to leave the books in the second-floor hallway until the inventory period is over.
evidence: "Ms. Maldonado, the same applies to the books in the second-floor hallway."

value.name: Rosa questions attorney's knowledge
value.description: Rosa is startled that the attorney knows about the books and asks how he knew.

value.name: attorney explains he observed Rosa
value.description: The attorney says he knew because he saw Rosa looking at the books the previous day.
evidence: "You were looking at them yesterday when we came down from the sewing room."

value.name: Rosa confirms books are inscribed
value.description: Rosa admits the books were a gift and confirms they are inscribed.
evidence: "They were a gift to you. I would not be surprised to learn that they were inscribed."

value.name: Rosa accepts inventory restriction
value.description: Rosa agrees to leave the books in place until the inventory is finished.
evidence: "Then they are, in all likelihood, yours, by the same logic. But they will be yours by agreement and not by removal in the meantime."

value.name: siblings choose appraiser
value.description: The siblings begin selecting an appraiser for the inventory process.

value.name: Daniel proposes familiar appraiser
value.description: Daniel suggests an appraiser whose name he recognizes from a real-estate transaction at his firm.
evidence: Daniel suggested the one whose name he recognized from a real-estate transaction he had handled at his firm

value.name: Lucia objects to appraiser choice
value.description: Lucia objects to Daniel's suggested appraiser on principle.

value.name: Rosa declines appraiser opinion
value.description: When asked, Rosa says she has no opinion about appraisers, though her statement is cut off in the excerpt.
